tasks.short: Keep job records and present a written progress report.

steps.what: Note actions on the job for the written record.
Maintain the hours and materials records for the job.
Retype those records into the office job file.
Draft the written progress report from the site notes.

loop.purpose: Turn the site note into a progress remark.
loop.input: Site note, hours, materials and photos already on the job.
loop.check: Every sentence names a site note, an hour line, a material or a photo on this job, and adds no defect the note does not state.
loop.stop: One pass. If the check fails, the remark stays blank and the carpenter writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Hours and checklist ticks are already fields. A template cannot phrase the remark from a free-text note.

steps.what: Check that progress report against the site notes.
Present the written progress report on site.
Accept the written progress report for this job.
File the accepted progress report on the job record.

tasks.design: The carpenter still notes actions on the job, enters hours and materials once, and presents the progress report on site. {ERP} keeps that entry as the job record, so the office does not retype it, and a draft remark is written from the site note only where every sentence points at a note, an hour, a material or a photo. The site supervisor still accepts the report before it is filed in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours were written on a sheet and typed again by the office, and the progress report was a fresh document.
tasks.enabler_now: The job system can store hours, materials, photos and checklist items. A short model pass can draft a remark that a person checks.
tasks.still_hard: The remark is only as good as the note. A missing photo or a vague note still needs the carpenter to write the line. The report must not become a score of the person.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what happened on the job, and refusing a remark that adds a defect the note does not state.

ambition.what: Close a checklist item the same day, while the work is still in front of the carpenter.

tasks.altitude: The carpenter still notes the work and presents the report. They confirm the remark. The office does not copy the hours. The site supervisor still accepts the report.

reach.task: Accept the weekly progress report for the job
reach.learn: Which actions, hours and defects the carpenter confirmed, and which remark lines were left blank.

evidence.claim: Syntess Atrium captures work orders, hours and materials on site.
PlanRadar logs defects and checklists and produces handover reports.
For Dutch consequence class 1, the contractor and an independent quality assurer build the completion file, and the contractor stays liable for defects found later.
Logging hours and jobs per worker observes presence and performance and needs works-council consent.
An AI system that allocates tasks from individual behaviour or personal traits, or that evaluates worker performance, is high-risk.

assumptions: The job record fields are job id, date, hours, material code, quantity, defect note, photo id and checklist item. The carpenter enters the note, hours and materials. The office used to retype them.
The draft remark may only use that entry. Checklist ticks are configured per job type. Upkeep of the checklist is about 1.2 hours per 100 hours of this task.

The report does not score or rank the carpenter, and it does not use van location. Where the building is in the Netherlands and in consequence class 1, the accepted report may enter the completion file.
unknowns: Whether this firm already has a job system that stores hours, photos and a checklist.
Whether this building is in Dutch consequence class 1, and who the quality assurer is.
Whether the works council has already consented to job-level hour logs.
research_questions: Does the current job system store hours, materials, photos and checklist items without a second typing?
Which progress-report lines does the completion file require for this building?

already_counted.description: Noting the work, entering hours and materials, checking the remark and presenting the report still take the carpenter's time.
The site supervisor still reads and accepts the progress report.

incremental.description: Update checklist items when the job type changes.

approvals.approved_version: Written progress report for this job and week, as the site supervisor accepted it. A later change voids the acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of jobs where the office no longer retypes hours and the remark is drafted from a clear site note. Noting the work, entering hours, checking the remark and presenting it stay. A week of vague notes, where the remark stays blank, sits at the low end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study plans, set the layout, and list materials.

steps.what: Study specifications in the blueprints and building plans.
List dimensions and materials the plans state.

loop.purpose: Copy stated dimensions and material callouts off the plan into a list.
loop.input: The current blueprint, sketch or building plan for this job.
loop.check: Every length and material on the list is a figure or callout visible on the named sheet, and no length is converted or inferred.
loop.stop: One pass. If any line has no figure on the sheet, the whole list stays blank.
loop.why_not_simpler: The plan is a drawing, not a table. A template cannot see a stated dimension.

steps.what: Check each stated dimension on the building plans.
Determine the project layout and the dimensions to cut.
Accept the layout and the materials required.
Mark that project layout on the site.
File the accepted materials list for the project.

tasks.design: The carpenter still studies the blueprints, decides the layout and marks it on site. A draft list copies only dimensions and materials stated on the sheet; if a line has no figure, the list stays blank. The site supervisor accepts the layout and the material list before the carpenter marks the site and before the list is filed in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dimensions were read off paper and copied by hand onto a cut list that could drift from the current sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Drawings are files. A model can copy a stated figure. It cannot decide a length that is not printed.
tasks.still_hard: Sketches, revisions and the site itself still need the carpenter. A copied figure can be from the wrong sheet.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding the layout and the dimension to cut, including where the drawing does not match the site.

ambition.what: Compare the layout with the current sheet before the first cut, on every job.

tasks.altitude: The carpenter still studies the plans, decides the layout and marks the site. A blank list means they take the figures themselves. The site supervisor still accepts the layout before it is marked.

reach.task: Order the materials for this carpentry job
reach.learn: Which materials the site supervisor accepted from the current drawings, and which lines were left blank.

evidence.claim: Copying a dimension that is printed on a drawing is a reading aid. Deciding the layout and the length to cut stays with the carpenter, because a wrong length is rework and can be unsafe.
A material list that names no person is ordinary project data. A note that identifies a worker is personal data and needs the firm's existing basis.

assumptions: The loop may copy sheet id, a stated length, its unit and a material callout. It may not compute, scale or infer a length.
If the sheet is a sketch with no clear figure, the list stays blank and the carpenter measures. The carpenter's study, layout decision and site mark stay.
Keeping the current sheet index is about 0.8 hours per 100 hours of this task. No product in the digest reads carpentry drawings, so this loop is model knowledge only.
unknowns: Whether this firm's drawings are current files with sheet numbers, or paper sketches.
Who must accept a layout before it is marked on a structural job.
research_questions: Are the current blueprints available as files with a sheet number the list can name?

already_counted.description: Studying the plans, checking stated dimensions, deciding the layout and marking the site still take the carpenter's time.
The site supervisor still accepts the layout and the material list.

incremental.description: Keep the current sheet index so the list names the sheet in force.

approvals.approved_version: Layout and material list for this job, taken from the current drawings, as the site supervisor accepted. A later change voids the acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A run of jobs with current drawings where stated dimensions are copied and then checked. Studying, deciding and marking stay. A run of sketches, where the list stays blank, sits at the low end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The carpenter still notes the work on site, studies the drawings, sets out the layout and presents the report. The office stops retyping hours. A draft remark and a draft dimension list are checked by the carpenter, and the site supervisor still accepts the report and the layout before they are filed.
reach: The site supervisor accepts the progress report and needs the confirmed notes, not a second paper diary.
The purchasing officer orders materials and needs the accepted list, including which lines were left blank.
skills_to_grow: Confirm a remark against the site note, and leave it blank when the note is vague.
Reject a dimension that is not printed on the current sheet.
Enter hours and materials once, on the job record.
role.ambitious_version: Each job has one record of hours, materials, photos and a progress remark the supervisor has accepted. The cut list starts from figures on the current drawing. The carpenter still sets out and builds.
